definition_basis: All variables are real and plane points are ordered real pairs. The positive coordinate-axis direction is left to right. Distance is |v-u| and is independent of endpoint order. Closed finite endpoints are included; open finite endpoints are excluded; infinity is never an included endpoint. Linear equations describe lines. Source 134 is proved from coordinate-axis unit lengths and segment additivity, not by assuming the distance formula being proved.

source_reviews.independent_solution: Let O have coordinate 0. If x_A=x_B, A=B, so |AB|=0=|x_B-x_A|. For x_A<x_B: when 0<=x_A<x_B, OB=OA+AB, so |AB|=x_B-x_A; when x_A<x_B<=0, OA=OB+AB, so |AB|=(-x_A)-(-x_B)=x_B-x_A; when x_A<0<x_B, O is between the endpoints and |AB|=|AO|+|OB|=-x_A+x_B=x_B-x_A. An endpoint at 0 is covered by the first two cases. Thus for x_A<=x_B the length is x_B-x_A=|x_B-x_A|. For x_A>x_B, interchange A and B to obtain |AB|=x_A-x_B=|x_B-x_A|. This covers all coordinate orders, signs and coincidence; the result is an unsigned length rather than a directed difference.
Distance between M(1.5) and M(-2) is |(-2)-1.5|=|-3.5|=3.5 coordinate units. The segment crosses 0 and its two lengths to the origin add to 1.5+2=3.5.
Distance between M(-10.3) and M(6.2) is |6.2-(-10.3)|=16.5 coordinate units. Opposite-sign coordinates put the origin between the endpoints, so their lengths to 0 add.
Distance between M(-3.6) and M(0) is |0-(-3.6)|=3.6 coordinate units, the length from -3.6 to the origin.
Distance between M(-5.7) and M(-7.1) is |(-7.1)-(-5.7)|=|-1.4|=1.4 coordinate units. Both points are on the negative ray, so the difference of their lengths to 0 is used, not the sum 5.7+7.1.

a) |x|=5 iff x=-5 or x=5, giving the two-point set {-5,5}, not an interval. b) |x|<5 iff -5<x<5, giving the open interval (-5,5), equivalently ]-5,5[. Both boundary points have distance exactly 5 and are excluded in b), while 0 is included.

a) |x-10|=4 iff x-10=-4 or 4, so x=6 or 14 and the solution set is {6,14}. b) |x-10|<=4 iff -4<=x-10<=4, so 6<=x<=14 and the solution set is [6,14]. Both boundary points and center 10 are included in b); a) contains only the two boundary points.

a) |x|>=5 iff x<=-5 OR x>=5, giving (-infinity,-5] union [5,+infinity). The finite endpoints are included and 0 is excluded. b) |x-10|>4 iff x-10<-4 OR x-10>4, hence x<6 OR x>14, giving (-infinity,6) union (14,+infinity). Finite endpoints 6 and 14 and center 10 are excluded. Each exterior set is a union of two rays, not their intersection.

The distance statement translates to |x-5|=2, equivalently |5-x|=2. It is equivalent to x-5=-2 or 2, hence x=3 or 7. The complete solution set is {3,7}; both values are exactly 2 from 5 and the interior points do not satisfy equality. Both the equation and solution set are part of the source task.

The statement translates to |a-(-1)|=|a+1|<3.5. Solving -3.5<a+1<3.5 gives -4.5<a<2.5. The solution set for a is (-4.5,2.5). Boundary points have distance exactly 3.5 and are excluded. The center is -1, not +1, and substituting a=-1 gives distance 0. Both the inequality and its solution set are required.

The statement translates to |y-(-4.5)|=|y+4.5|<=0.2. Solving -0.2<=y+4.5<=0.2 gives -4.7<=y<=-4.3. The solution set for y is [-4.7,-4.3]. Boundary points are included because 'not greater than' includes equality; y=-4.5 has distance 0. Both the inequality and its solution set are required.

The moving coordinate is -b. Distance from -12 is |(-b)-(-12)|=|12-b|=|b-12|. 'Not less than 1/48' translates to |b-12|>=1/48. Therefore b-12<=-1/48 OR b-12>=1/48, giving b<=575/48 OR b>=577/48. The solution set for b is (-infinity,575/48] union [577/48,+infinity). At b=575/48 and b=577/48 the moving coordinates are -12+1/48 and -12-1/48, so both endpoints satisfy equality and are included. At b=12 the distance is 0 and it is excluded. Because the point coordinate is -b, the center in variable b is +12, not -12. The solution is closed exterior, not interior; the translated inequality and full set are both required.

a) Over the reals, (x-2)(y+3)=0 iff x=2 OR y=-3. The set is the union of the complete vertical line x=2 and complete horizontal line y=-3, including their intersection (2,-3), not just that point. Textual plot: draw both full solid lines extending both ways; (2,0) and (0,-3) belong and (0,0) does not. b) The rational expression (y-x)/(x-1) must be defined, so x!=1; it equals zero iff y-x=0. The set is {(x,y): y=x, x!=1}, the line y=x with only (1,1) removed. Textual plot: draw the full line through (0,0) and (2,2), extending both ways, with an open hole at (1,1). At (1,1) the expression is undefined 0/0, not zero. The nonzero denominator condition must not be discarded. These are complete textual specifications of the requested planar representations; no drawing image or visible-choice fidelity judgment is supplied in stage1.
